Note on this article: Each unit's slots are further broken down by trade (e.g. Electrician, Fitter, Welder, Carpenter, Painter, Diesel Mechanic, etc.) and by category (UR/OBC/SC/ST/EWS), with separate reserved slots for PwBD (Persons with Benchmark Disability) and Ex-servicemen, set out in detailed tables for each of the 8 units in the official notification. Given the scale of this breakdown (dozens of trade rows across 8 separate unit tables), this article presents unit-level totals only; candidates must check the official notification for the exact trade-wise and category-wise slot count for their chosen unit and trade before applying, since a candidate may only select a unit where a training slot exists for their specific ITI trade.

When the prescribed number of SC or ST candidates are not available, those reserved training places may be filled by the other of the two (SC by ST, or vice versa); if still unfilled, they may be filled by candidates not belonging to SC/ST. Similarly, seats remaining unfilled by OBC/EWS candidates will be filled by unreserved category candidates. Reserved PwBD and Ex-servicemen seats are not separate or additional - they are already included within the total slots shown for each trade.

NWR Act Apprentice Eligibility Criteria

NWR Act Apprentice Qualification

Candidates must have passed the Class 10 examination or its equivalent (under the 10+2 examination system) with a minimum of 50% marks in aggregate (no rounding off) from a recognised Board, and must also possess a National Trade Certificate (NTC) in the notified trade, issued by the National Council for Vocational Training (NCVT) or State Council for Vocational Training (SCVT). Candidates should have the requisite educational/technical qualification from a recognised Board/Government University/Institute as on the date of submission of the application; those awaiting results of their final exams should not apply.

NWR Act Apprentice Reservation Details

Candidates claiming SC/ST reservation must produce a caste certificate in the Central Government format at the time of Document Verification. OBC candidates must produce a caste certificate and a Non-Creamy Layer Certificate issued on or after 1 April 2026, in the Central Government format, along with an OBC declaration. EWS candidates must produce an EWS certificate in the prescribed format. Ex-servicemen and Armed Forces Personnel (or their children) must produce a discharge certificate, or an Armed Forces serving certificate in the case of children of serving personnel, at the time of Document Verification. Ex-servicemen candidates are placed in their appropriate category (UR/SC/ST/OBC); if UR vacancies under the Ex-servicemen quota are unavailable, Ex-servicemen belonging to communities where vacancies are available will be considered.

NWR Act Apprentice Age Limit

Particulars Age
Minimum Age 15 years (completed)
Maximum Age 24 years (not completed)

NWR Act Apprentice Age Relaxation

  • SC/ST candidates: 5 years' relaxation in upper age limit.
  • OBC candidates: 3 years' relaxation in upper age limit.
  • Persons with Benchmark Disability (PwBD): 10 years' relaxation in upper age limit.
  • Ex-servicemen: relaxable by up to an additional 10 years, to the extent of service rendered in the Defence Forces plus 3 years, provided a minimum of 6 months' continuous service was completed (this does not apply to ex-servicemen who have already joined government service on the civil side after availing ex-servicemen status for that engagement).

NWR Act Apprentice Stipend & Training

Training period and stipend will be as per the extant rules and directives issued by the Railway Board from time to time; a specific stipend amount is not stated in this notification. No hostel accommodation will be provided - selected candidates must make their own arrangements during training, as per the Apprentices Act, 1961, and will be released upon completion of training. Before commencing training, the selected candidate (or their guardian, if a minor) must enter into a Contract of Apprenticeship with the employer.

NWR Act Apprentice Application Fee

Category Application Fee (Non-refundable)
All candidates except those listed below ₹100
SC/ST, Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD), Women Nil

Fee payment is made online through the payment gateway integrated with the online application, using debit card, credit card, Internet Banking, or similar modes, after the application form is completed and verified for correctness; no change/edit is allowed after fee payment. Any transaction charges for online payment are borne by the candidate. On successful payment, an e-receipt is generated, which should be printed and retained.

NWR Act Apprentice Selection Process

Selection is based on a merit list prepared for all candidates who apply against the notification, calculated as the simple average of the percentage of marks in Matriculation (minimum 50% aggregate) and the percentage of marks in ITI, in the trade in which apprenticeship is sought.

  • For Matriculation percentage, marks obtained by the candidate in all subjects are considered - not the marks of any single subject or group of subjects.
  • For ITI percentage, marks mentioned in the provisional/final certificate are considered.
  • In case two candidates have the same marks, the older candidate is preferred; if the date of birth is also the same, the candidate who passed the Matriculation exam earlier is considered first.
  • The final merit list is prepared division/unit-wise, trade-wise, and community-wise, equal to the number of slots, in descending order of the percentage of marks obtained.
  • Candidates finally enlisted are subject to verification of original testimonials and production of a medical certificate (as per the notification's Annexure-IV).

Candidates should note that no centralised merit list is formed - each unit's merit list is prepared separately based on candidates who applied for that specific unit.

Medical Fitness

Selected candidates must produce a medical certificate in the prescribed format at the time of Document Verification, signed by a Government-authorised Gazetted Doctor not below the rank of Assistant Surgeon of a Central/State Hospital. Standards of fitness for Persons with Disability are also specified in the notification, covering Locomotor Disability/Cerebral Palsy (not less than 40% relevant disability), Hearing Impairment (loss of 60 decibels or more in the better ear, including Deaf, Dumb, or Deaf & Dumb candidates), and other benchmark disability categories as defined in the notification.

How to Apply for NWR Act Apprentice Recruitment 2026

NWR Act Apprentice Apply Online

Candidates must apply online only, by visiting www.rrcjaipur.in, between 7 October 2026 and 6 November 2026 (23:59 hrs). No physical copy of the application needs to be sent to RRC, and any physical copy received will not be given cognisance. The broad process is:

  1. Log in and fill personal details: Log on to the RRC/Jaipur website and carefully fill in personal details/bio-data, including a valid 12-digit Aadhaar Card number (the original Aadhaar card must be produced at Document Verification).
  2. Select one unit only: Candidates must choose only one Division/Unit from the 8 listed, and should carefully check that a training slot exists for their specific ITI trade in that unit before selecting it, since changes are not allowed after final submission.
  3. Upload photograph: A recent colour photograph (3.5 cm × 3.5 cm, not older than 3 months, JPG/JPEG format, 100 DPI, file size 20 KB–70 KB) with a clear front view, without cap or sunglasses.
  4. Upload signature: A scanned signature (3.5 cm × 2.5 cm, JPG/JPEG format, 100 DPI, file size 20 KB–30 KB).
  5. Pay the application fee: Pay the applicable fee (see Fee section above) through the integrated payment gateway, after verifying that all application details are correct, since no changes are allowed after payment.
  6. Download and retain printout: After successful submission, download and keep a printout of the application; this will be required at the time of Document Verification, if shortlisted.

Candidates must ensure their name, father's name, and date of birth exactly match their Matriculation (or equivalent) certificate - any deviation found during Document Verification will lead to cancellation of candidature and debarment. Candidates should also provide an active mobile number and valid email ID, since all important communication will be sent via SMS/email.

NWR Act Apprentice Important Instructions

  • Candidates may apply for only one unit; submitting more than one application with different particulars (name, father's name, community, photo, qualification, email, or mobile number) will result in summary rejection of all such applications.
  • The decision of the Railway administration on all matters relating to eligibility, acceptance or rejection of applications, and mode of selection is final.
  • Imparting training on the Railway does not confer any right to absorption/employment on the Railway after successful completion of training; per the Apprenticeship Rules, 1992, it is not obligatory for the employer to offer employment, nor for the apprentice to accept it, upon completion of training.
  • No correspondence regarding engagement will be entertained.
  • Canvassing in any form will disqualify the candidature, and no correspondence will be entertained in this regard.
  • Candidates should ensure they fulfil all eligibility criteria before applying; if erroneously engaged, such candidates will be summarily dismissed without notice at any stage.
  • For help with online submission or printing of the application, candidates can call the helpline number published on the website from 7 October 2026, available 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM (except Sundays and holidays) until the last date of application.

Candidates can log in with their Registration Number and Date of Birth to see their allotted exam city. CBT 1 is scheduled for 3, 4 and 5 November 2026. The city slip is not the admit card, and it cannot be used for entry to the exam hall.

How to Download the RRB ALP City Intimation Slip

Follow these steps on the official exam portal or your regional RRB website.

  3. Click Login and enter your Registration Number and Date of Birth.
  4. Enter the captcha and click Submit.
  5. Your exam city, exam date and shift will appear on the screen. Check every detail.
  6. Download the slip and keep a copy for reference.

If you see a message that the slip is not live, it usually means your exam date has a later release date. Check the date-wise schedule above and try again on your release date.

Once you download the slip, check the following details carefully.

  • Candidate name and registration number
  • Allotted exam city and state
  • Exam date and shift
  • Reporting time, gate closing time and exam start time
  • General instructions for the exam day

The slip names only the city. The exact exam centre address is given on the admit card.

RRB ALP CBT 1 Shift Timings

CBT 1 is held in three shifts a day, and each shift lasts 60 minutes. The timings below are indicative. Your exact shift and reporting time are printed on your slip and admit card, so follow those.

Shift 1 7:30 AM 8:30 AM 9:00 AM 10:00 AM

Candidates are not allowed to enter after the gate closes, so plan to reach the centre well before the reporting time.

RRB ALP CBT 1 Exam Pattern

CBT 1 is a screening test. It has 75 questions for 75 marks, to be completed in 60 minutes. The questions come from Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning, General Science and General Awareness. Marking scheme details beyond this are Not Available Officially in the information checked for this article. Candidates should refer to the official CEN 01/2026 notification for the full scheme.

RRB ALP Selection Process

The selection of Assistant Loco Pilots under CEN 01/2026 has these stages.

  1. Computer Based Test 1 (CBT 1)
  2. Computer Based Test 2 (CBT 2)
  3. Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)
  4. Document Verification
  5. Medical Examination

The process is currently at the first stage, CBT 1. Dates for the later stages are Not Yet Announced.

RRB ALP Admit Card 2026: When Will It Be Released?

The official admit card date is Not Yet Announced. RRBs usually release the admit card (e-call letter) about four days before the exam date mentioned on the city slip. The admit card will carry the exact centre address, reporting time, your photo and signature, and exam day instructions. Download it from the same login using your Registration Number and Date of Birth once the link is active.

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Download the city slip only from the official portal or your regional RRB website.
  • Check your name, registration number, exam date and city. If anything looks wrong, contact your RRB through its official grievance channel.
  • Do not treat the city slip as an entry pass. Carry your admit card and a valid photo ID to the exam centre.
  • Plan your travel and stay as soon as you know your city, but wait for the admit card for the exact centre address.
  • Reach the centre before the gate closing time. Late entry is not allowed.
  • Whether a change of exam city is allowed is Not Available Officially in the details checked for this article.

  • Candidates must have passed Class 10th with 2 years of technical training from ITI.   • Candidates must have passed Class 10th with 2 years of technical training from ITI. Alternatively, candidates can have a 2 or 3-year Diploma in Instrument Mechanic, Instrument Technology, Electronic Mechanic, or Electronic Technology from a recognized institution.

An expert committee set up by the examination conducting authority reviews all objections. Its decision is final and binding, and no further objections are heard at any level.

About UPSC Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination 2026

The ISS Examination is one of the premier competitive exams conducted by UPSC to recruit officers for Group A and Group B posts in the Indian Statistical Service. Understanding the exam structure helps candidates correctly interpret the provisional answer key.

The Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination is conducted annually by the Union Public Service Commission to fill vacancies in the Indian Statistical Service, one of India's organised Group A Central Services. The exam tests candidates on subjects including Statistics, General English, and General Studies. The Statistics papers are the most technical and weightage-heavy components of the exam. The provisional answer key released covers the objective/multiple-choice components of the Statistics papers.

ISS Examination Paper Structure

The ISS Examination 2026 Statistics papers for which the provisional answer key has been released are:

  • Statistics Paper I - Covers topics such as Probability, Statistical Methods, Numerical Analysis, and related areas.
  • Statistics Paper II - Covers topics including Linear Models, Statistical Inference, Sampling Theory, and Econometrics.

How to Raise Objections Against UPSC ISS Provisional Answer Key 2026

If a candidate disagrees with any answer published in the provisional answer key, they can submit a formal representation to UPSC within the stipulated objection window period.

UPSC allows candidates to challenge answers in the provisional answer key by submitting a formal representation. The process for raising objections is as follows:

  • Download the provisional answer key PDF for the relevant paper.
  • Identify the question number(s) where you believe the answer is incorrect.
  • Prepare a written representation with supporting references from standard textbooks or study material.
  • Submit the representation to UPSC through the official channel specified in the answer key notification (typically by post or online submission to the UPSC office).
  • UPSC will review all representations received before publishing the Final Answer Key.

What Happens After the Provisional Answer Key?

After the provisional answer key is released and the objection window closes, UPSC reviews all valid representations before publishing the Final Answer Key.

Once the objection period ends, UPSC's subject matter experts review all representations submitted by candidates. Valid objections where an answer is found to be incorrect based on credible references result in changes to the final answer key. The Final Answer Key is then published on the official website. The final marks are computed based on the final (not provisional) answer key, which forms the basis for merit list preparation and eventual selection to the Indian Statistical Service.

Post Name Qualification
Primary Teacher
  • Senior Secondary (or its equivalent) with at least 50% marks and a 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education (D.El.Ed./BTC). OR
  • Senior Secondary (or its equivalent) with at least 45% marks and a 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education (D.El.Ed./BTC) obtained in accordance with the NCTE (Recognition, Norms and Procedure) Regulations, 2002. OR
  • Senior Secondary (or its equivalent) with at least 50% marks and a 4-year Bachelor of Elementary Education (B.El.Ed.). OR
  • Senior Secondary (or its equivalent) with at least 50% marks and a 2-year Diploma in Education (Special Education) (D.Ed. Special Education) recognized by the Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI). OR
  • Graduation (or its equivalent) along with a 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education (D.El.Ed./BTC).
  • Government Primary School Shiksha Mitras working on an honorarium basis who, with the permission of the State Government, have successfully completed the 2-year D.El.Ed. programme from Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU).
  • Regularly appointed Assistant Teachers/Head Teachers (Primary) and Assistant Teachers/Head Teachers (Upper Primary) serving in all categories of schools allotted a DISE Code and teaching Classes 1 to 5 (in-service teachers).
Upper Primary Teacher
  • Graduation (or its equivalent) along with a 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education (BTC/D.El.Ed.). OR
  • Graduation (or its equivalent) with at least 50% marks and a 1-year Bachelor of Education (B.Ed./L.T./Shiksha Shastri) (Regular/Institutional only). OR
  • Graduation (or its equivalent) with at least 45% marks and a 1-year Bachelor of Education (B.Ed./L.T./Shiksha Shastri) (Regular/Institutional only), obtained in accordance with the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) Regulations issued from time to time. OR
  • Senior Secondary (10+2) or its equivalent with at least 50% marks and a 4-year Bachelor of Elementary Education (B.El.Ed.). OR
  • Senior Secondary (10+2) or its equivalent with at least 50% marks and a 4-year B.A. B.Ed. / B.Sc. B.Ed. integrated degree. OR
  • Graduation (or its equivalent) with at least 50% marks and a B.Ed. (Special Education) recognized by the Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI). OR
